name: Polar & High Seas
blurb: The polar regions and the open ocean: melting ice and thawing ground, a sea turning more acid, and industry heading for the deep seabed, the krill and the boreal forest.

issues.title: The Deep-Sea Gold Rush

drivers.name: Weak rules on the high seas

fact.text: The International Seabed Authority’s contract list shows 32 exploration contracts, one of which (held by CPRM) renounced its rights in December 2021; 19 are for polymetallic nodules, 17 of them in the Clarion–Clipperton Fracture Zone.

issues.realWorld: Ask the companies that make your phone, car and battery whether they will source metal from the deep seabed, and support recycling and the call for a moratorium.

issues.title: The Oil Sands and the Boreal

drivers.name: Seismic lines that fragment the forest

fact.text: An Environmental Defence and CPAWS report found that as of 2020 the total volume of Alberta’s oil sands tailings “ponds” was estimated at 1.4 trillion litres, and the total tailings area was over 300 km² in 2020.
fact.source: Environmental Defence and CPAWS, “50 Years of Sprawling Tailings” (May 2022)

issues.realWorld: Support Indigenous-led conservation areas, ask whether your pension or bank funds new extraction projects, and use less fossil fuel where you can.

issues.title: Krill: The Base of the Food Web

drivers.name: Concentrated krill catches near penguin colonies
No agreed way to spread the catch

fact.text: The Antarctic krill fishery closed early for the second year in a row on 12 August 2026 after reaching its 620,000-tonne trigger level; CCAMLR’s secretariat reported that the trigger was first reached on 1 August 2025, after the lapse of conservation measure 51-07 changed how the fishery was spread in space and time.
fact.source: CCAMLR Secretariat, SC-CAMLR-44/BG/36 Rev. 2 (2025), and Mongabay (August 2026)

also.source: The Fish Site (14 August 2026), on the 2026 closure

issues.realWorld: Check that krill-oil and fish-feed products come from certified, precautionary sources, and support the call for a Southern Ocean sanctuary.

issues.title: The Acid Sea

drivers.name: Carbon dioxide absorbed by the ocean
Cold water that absorbs more CO₂
Added stress from warming and pollution

fact.text: The 2025 Planetary Health Check found that seven of nine planetary boundaries are now breached, with ocean acidification breached for the first time; NOAA says the surface ocean’s pH has fallen by 0.1 units since the industrial era, about a 30 percent increase in acidity, and pteropods are showing signs of shell damage.
fact.source: Stockholm University, reporting the Planetary Health Check 2025 (25 September 2025)

issues.realWorld: Cutting your own carbon emissions helps, as does supporting policies that reduce them; ocean acidification follows the carbon dioxide we put into the air.

issues.title: The Emperor Penguins’ Ice

fact.text: A 2023 study in Communications Earth & Environment found that in 2022 four of the five emperor penguin breeding sites in the central and eastern Bellingshausen Sea region had total breeding failure, because sea ice broke up before the chicks could grow waterproof feathers.
fact.source: Fretwell et al., Communications Earth & Environment (2023), “Record low 2022 Antarctic sea ice led to catastrophic breeding failure of emperor penguins”

also.source: NBC News (24 August 2023), reporting the study

issues.realWorld: Cutting your own carbon emissions and backing policies that cut them is the main lever; you can also support colony monitoring projects that track penguins from satellites.

issues.title: The Thawing Ground

fact.text: The US National Snow and Ice Data Center says scientists estimate about 1,400 gigatons of carbon are frozen in permafrost, about 2.5 times the roughly 850 gigatons in the atmosphere, and that thawing releases carbon dioxide and methane.

issues.realWorld: Cutting your own carbon emissions and backing policies that cut them is the main lever, since thaw releases carbon dioxide and methane.

issues.title: Plastic at the Pole

fact.text: The Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Programme says microplastics have been found in Arctic snow, sea-ice, seawater and sediments collected on the ocean floor, that whales, fish and birds can ingest larger pieces, and that the plastic pollution tide is also rising in the Arctic.
fact.source: AMAP Litter and Microplastics Expert Group

issues.realWorld: Use less single-use plastic, support a strong global plastics treaty, and take part in shoreline cleanups.
